Shape: Involved — the fix is small, but recording a branch earlier also affects fresh-claim base advancement.

## What we know
- `ClaimCheckpointFrom` already prefers recorded state over the title (`internal/workspace/worktree.go:96`). Explicit claim, automatic selection, and work pass that state (`internal/cli/claim.go:103`, `internal/cli/selection.go:175`, `internal/workflow/engine.go:639`).
- `Manager.acquire` saves a claim without initializing Branch (`internal/lease/manager.go:915`); `RecordCheckpoint` sets it later (`:1803`). Thus an uncheckpointed task can be re-provisioned using an edited title.
- `freshClaimBase` currently treats any Branch as evidence of prior work (`internal/lease/claim_base.go:23`). A reserved name must not disable existing untouched-base advancement.
- Reapproval on a base containing the checkpoint moves its identity to `DroppedCheckpoint` and clears Branch/HeadSHA (`internal/lease/manager.go:708-713`). Recovery provisions the retained branch (`internal/workspace/recovery.go:20`); `RecordCheckpoint` requires that same identity (`internal/lease/manager.go:1791-1799`).
- Fork acquisition clears prior same-repository branch state except for same-contributor budget recovery (`internal/lease/manager.go:1033-1038`).
- Edit reads authoritative state and renders text/JSON previews (`internal/cli/issue_edit.go:101`); active claims are intentionally refused (`:261`). Title edits require separate approval; preserve both restrictions.

## Implementation
1. Modify `internal/lease/manager.go`, `Manager.acquire`: after existing approval/base preparation and checkpoint cleanup, reserve an empty same-repository issue Branch before the existing CAS save: use `DroppedCheckpoint.Branch` when `DroppedCheckpoint != nil`; otherwise use `workspace.BranchName(n, issue.Title)`. Never replace a retained recovery identity with a title-derived name. Apply only to issue claims, preserving PR revision behavior. Preserve nonempty recorded branches, checkpoint heads, PR revisions, fork claim naming, and failed-CAS behavior. Do not publish or rename branches.
2. Modify `internal/lease/claim_base.go`, `freshClaimBase`: a same-repository reserved Branch without HeadSHA must remain eligible under the existing artifact, fork, PR, policy, ancestry, and human-gate checks. Extend `internal/lease/claim_base_test.go` and `internal/lease/manager_test.go` for first claim, release/reclaim, title edit/reapproval, existing branch preservation, and CAS failure. Keep checkpoint-backed and dropped-checkpoint states ineligible. Extend `internal/lease/manager_test.go:419` for N2: same-repo acquire reserves a branch, release, then fork acquire must clear that reservation and `ClaimCheckpointFrom` must return `ForkBranchName(issue, newClaimID)`, not the reserved name. Preserve budget-resume behavior.
3. Modify `internal/cli/issue_edit.go`, `issueEditPreview` and rendering: when a title changes and state has a branch, report its exact name and that it remains unchanged, in text and JSON. Extend `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go`: preview performs no writes; actual edit followed by approval and claim/work retains the original branch, both before and after a plan checkpoint. Exercise local coordination and the existing GitHub HTTP/bare-origin fixture (`TestIssueEditBackendGitHub`). Extend `internal/workflow/engine_test.go` for work reuse using mock agents. For R1, extend `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go` using the recovery setup in `internal/lease/recovery_publication_test.go:18` and `internal/workspace/recovery_test.go:11`: checkpoint → release → title edit → reapprove on a base containing the checkpoint head → claim → stage. Assert reapproval stores the original dropped identity, acquire reserves its branch, the worktree stays on that branch, and stage/RecordCheckpoint succeeds and clears pending recovery. Use a temporary bare origin where publication identity is required; retain ancestry and remote-head refusal tests.
4. Modify `docs/developer.md:43` with one sentence explaining branch retention after title edits. Add the issue-218 changelog fragment described below. No protected files change.

## Design choice
Reserve the branch in authoritative state at first claim; warning plus later adoption would leave more title-sensitive paths. Reuse the existing Branch field and CAS rather than adding a schema or trusting checkout names.

## What we’re assuming
The shared lease manager should cover both backends; the local and GitHub regression fixtures will verify that.

## Open questions
Historical states with an empty Branch cannot identify an old title-derived branch from state alone; do not infer authority from an arbitrary checkout. If acceptance requires recovering such pre-fix states, reopen the plan for a bounded, verified migration rather than silently adopting a branch.

## HANDOFF
- Entry points and changes are listed above; preserve claim/work call sites and `ClaimCheckpointFrom` unchanged. Extend `TestClaimCheckpointFrom` in `internal/workspace/upstream_remote_test.go:91` only if additional recorded-name coverage is needed.
- N1 consumers to verify, preserve unchanged unless the reservation requires a directly related expectation update: `internal/cli/status.go:105` emits a Checkpoint block for Branch without HeadSHA; `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go:82` and `internal/lease/cleanup_preview.go:76,103,125` enumerate recorded local/remote branches; `internal/cli/stage.go:254` and `internal/cli/submit.go:136` select the recorded branch. Branch-only state already exists via `internal/lease/checkpoint_discard.go:87`; preserve inspection, cleanup eligibility, and publication fences. Run Status, Cleanup, Stage and Submit tests in the focused filter.
- What this change breaks: update branch-only expectations in `TestFreshClaimBase` and `TestFreshClaimBaseEarlyErrors` (`internal/lease/claim_base_test.go:19,256`); preserve fork, checkpoint discard, recovery, fencing, and `TestIssueStateProvisionContext` behavior. Preserve existing issue-edit approval/refusal tests and README command table (`README.md:251`); no CLI flags, templates, or schemas change. Update only the developer-guide paragraph noted above.
- Only proposed file addition (base absence unresolved): `changes/unreleased/218-stable-task-branch.md` is absent in the supplied snapshot (`test ! -e` succeeded). No Git metadata is exposed, so approved-base absence cannot be confirmed here. Before creating it, the developer must run `git cat-file -e "$base_sha:changes/unreleased/218-stable-task-branch.md"`; if present, modify it instead. No other added files are planned.
- Follow the exact focused verification commands in TEST_PLAN.md in order (build, package vet, targeted tests, then the sole full suite via make check). Developers write only source, tests, docs/changelog, IMPLEMENTATION.md and LESSONS.md; leave other active artifacts untouched. Reopen for a new state schema, fork protocol change, unsafe legacy adoption, or required branch renaming. This fits the 16-hour claim budget.

# Verification

1. **Acceptance 1 — recorded branch survives title edits:** add regressions in `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go` and `internal/workflow/engine_test.go` named with `TitleEdit` or `RecordedBranch`. Create/approve/claim, save the original branch, release, edit title, reapprove, then claim or work with mock agents. Assert success, original worktree branch, state.Branch equality, and no replacement branch. Cover local and GitHub (HTTP fixture plus temporary bare origin), uncheckpointed and planned tasks. Extend lease tests for reservation, preservation, fresh-base advancement, and CAS failure; retain fork/PR isolation tests. **R1:** checkpoint → release → title edit → reapprove on a base containing the head → claim/stage, asserting original Branch and worktree branch, successful RecordCheckpoint, and cleared DroppedCheckpoint. Assert the dropped identity exists after approval and is used during acquire; the test must fail with title-only reservation. **N2:** same-repository reservation → release → fork acquire; assert the old reservation is cleared and provisioning selects ForkBranchName for the new claim ID. Name these regressions with RecordedBranch so the filter includes them.
2. **Acceptance 2 — dry-run notice:** extend `TestIssueEdit` cases for text and JSON containing the exact recorded branch and retention notice. Assert no tracker/state/ref writes; cover missing branch and active-claim refusal without weakening approval rules.
3. **Acceptance 3 — make check:** after formatting only changed Go files, run commands below. `make check` includes the sole full race-enabled suite; do not also run `go test ./...`. Run approved static checks directly as needed without repeating the full suite.
4. **N1 consumers:** exercise existing Status, Cleanup, Stage and Submit tests for Branch-without-HeadSHA state; preserve inspection and cleanup safety rather than treating a reservation as a published checkpoint.
5. **Constraint/docs:** inspect the changelog entry; confirm approved-base absence before creation as described in PLAN.md. Check the changed developer-guide paragraph and its links; it introduces no commands or flags.

```bash

go vet ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow ./internal/workspace
```

Planning verification uses existing tests only; it does not establish coverage for the proposed fix. Record results separately from implementation acceptance. The sandbox has no repository Git metadata; historical-base checks require the normal developer checkout, not invented base evidence.

Planning baseline results (this revision): `go build ./...` passed; the focused-package `go vet` command above passed; the exact targeted test command above passed for all four packages (lease 29.073s, CLI 93.402s, workflow 4.480s, workspace 33.211s). No full suite is run during planning; reserve it for make check after implementation.

## Findings (non-blocking; developer should handle in implementation)

1. **Fresh-start states and `freshClaimBase`.** `checkpoint_discard.go:84-87` already leaves `Branch = FreshStartBranch(...)`, `HeadSHA = ""` and `FreshStart != nil`. If `freshClaimBase` is relaxed to accept any same-repository "Branch without HeadSHA", that post-discard state also becomes eligible for automatic base advancement, which it currently is not. The plan says to preserve checkpoint-discard behavior, so keep `st.FreshStart != nil` ineligible (or justify the change) and include it in the `TestFreshClaimBase` table.
2. **Reservation ordering.** `fresh` is computed before `prepareClaimBase` (`manager.go:848-866`). Reserve only after that point, as the plan states, so the reservation never affects freshness for the current claim. Do not reserve on PR-revision or fork acquires.
3. **Status for reserved-only state.** `status.go:105` will now show a Checkpoint block for every claimed issue (with empty HeadSHA). Confirm that the existing Status tests still describe this state accurately. Update an expectation only if it is directly caused by the reservation.

# Implementation Summary (Issue #218)

## What we learned

- Claims record the task branch in state now; tests that provision a worktree with a made-up title or branch and then call `RecordCheckpoint` must pass the claim's `st.Branch`, or they fail with "checkpoint branch differs from approved branch".

## Developer report

# Implementation: ISSUE-218 — title edits keep the recorded task branch

## What changed

1. `internal/lease/manager.go` (`Manager.acquire`): after the fork reset and right before the lease and CAS save, a same-repository issue claim (`prNumber == 0`) with an empty `Branch` now reserves one. It uses `DroppedCheckpoint.Branch` when a recovery identity is pending (R1). Otherwise it uses `workspace.BranchName(n, issue.Title)`. Existing branches, PR revisions, and fork claims (`AcquireFork`, a separate path) are untouched. The reservation happens after `freshClaimBase`/`prepareClaimBase`, so it never affects freshness for the current claim (review finding 2). A failed CAS saves nothing.
2. `internal/lease/claim_base.go` (`freshClaimBase`): a branch reserved without a checkpoint still counts as untouched, so it no longer blocks fresh-base advancement. These states stay ineligible: `HeadSHA`, `FreshStart` (post-discard, review finding 1), `ResumeCheckpointBranch`, a fork, a PR, submitted heads, and `DroppedCheckpoint`.
3. `internal/cli/issue_edit.go`: the preview gains `task_branch` and `task_branch_note` (JSON) and a `Task branch: <name> (task branch stays as recorded; the title edit does not rename it)` text line. These appear only when the title changes and state records a branch, or a pending recovery branch the next claim will reserve. Approval and active-claim refusal are unchanged.
4. `docs/developer.md`: one paragraph under "Revise a WorkUnit". `changes/unreleased/218-stable-task-branch.md`: a changelog fragment.

`ClaimCheckpointFrom` and the claim/work call sites are unchanged. They already preferred the recorded branch.

## Tests

- `internal/lease/claim_base_test.go`: in `TestFreshClaimBase`, `branch` now advances the base and keeps `existing`. A new `fresh start` case does not advance. Every case asserts the reserved branch. In `TestFreshClaimBaseEarlyErrors`, the `resumed stale` case now has a checkpoint head, so it still exercises a non-fresh state, as originally intended.
- `internal/lease/recorded_branch_test.go` (new): survives title edit plus reapproval; nothing saved on CAS failure; N2 fork after a reservation (Branch cleared, `ClaimCheckpointFrom` picks `ForkBranchName(issue, newClaimID)`); R1 at lease level with the Git store and bare origin (checkpoint → release → title edit → reapprove on a base containing the head → acquire reserves the dropped branch → `RecordCheckpoint` consumes the recovery).
- `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go`: `TestIssueEditTitleEditRecordedBranch` (uncheckpointed and planned: claim → release → dry-run notice → edit → approve → `issue claim` → `issue work`, all on the original branch and worktree, with no renamed branch created); `TestIssueEditTitleEditRecordedBranchDroppedCheckpoint` (R1 end to end: claim → checkpoint → release → title edit → new base → approve → claim → stage plan, review-plan, stage implement; the recovery is consumed on the original branch); `TestIssueEditDryRunRecordedBranch` (recorded, missing, title unchanged, and active claim, in text and JSON, with no state or tracker writes). `TestIssueEditBackendGitHub` now stores a recorded branch and asserts the notice over the GitHub HTTP fixture with a bare origin.
- `internal/workflow/recorded_branch_test.go` (new): `ExecuteWork` with mock agents reuses the branch and worktree after a title edit plus reapproval.
- Mutation checks: with the dropped-checkpoint preference removed, both R1 tests fail (`claim reserved "swarm/issue-1-renamed-task"`). With the reservation disabled, every AC1/AC2 regression fails.
- Fixture updates caused by the change (tests recorded checkpoints on names production never provisions): `internal/lease/revoke_test.go` (2 tests used `swarm/issue-1-<claimID>`) and `internal/cli/checkpoint_reconcile_test.go` / `issue_discard_checkpoint_test.go` (provisioned with title `"test"`). They now use the claim's recorded branch, as `claim.go` does.

## N1 consumers

These were not modified and were exercised by the Status/Cleanup/Stage/Submit filter, which passes. `status.go:105` now shows the Checkpoint block (branch, empty head) for a reserved-only claim. No existing Status test expectation changed. Cleanup enumerates the recorded branch as before. A branch-only state already existed after discard.

## Notes

- Approved-base absence of the changelog file could not be checked with `git cat-file`: the snapshot has no Git metadata (`fatal: not a git repository`). The file is absent in the snapshot, so it was created.
- Legacy states claimed before this fix still have an empty Branch until their next claim, which then reserves from the current title (open question in PLAN; no migration added).

## HANDOFF

**Changed behavior:** the first same-repository issue claim records the task branch (or the pending recovery branch) in state, so later title edits do not change the branch that claim/work provision. A reserved branch without a checkpoint does not block fresh-base advancement. `issue edit` previews report the recorded branch when the title changes.

**Changed files:** `internal/lease/manager.go`, `internal/lease/claim_base.go`, `internal/cli/issue_edit.go`, `docs/developer.md`, `changes/unreleased/218-stable-task-branch.md`; tests: `internal/lease/claim_base_test.go`, `internal/lease/recorded_branch_test.go` (new), `internal/lease/revoke_test.go`, `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go`, `internal/cli/checkpoint_reconcile_test.go`, `internal/cli/issue_discard_checkpoint_test.go`, `internal/workflow/recorded_branch_test.go` (new).

# Validation: ISSUE-218 — title edits keep the recorded task branch

**Provisional verdict: PASS** (advisory; the coordinator reruns the required checks authoritatively).

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC1: after a title edit, `issue work` and `issue claim` use the recorded branch and succeed; covered by tests | Verified | `internal/lease/manager.go:886-895` reserves `Branch` on the first same-repo issue claim (`prNumber == 0`, `Branch == ""`), preferring `DroppedCheckpoint.Branch`. The reservation runs after `freshClaimBase`/`prepareClaimBase` (`:848-866`). Regressions: `TestIssueEditTitleEditRecordedBranch` (CLI claim and work, uncheckpointed and planned), `TestExecuteWorkTitleEditRecordedBranch` (workflow), `TestAcquireRecordedBranchSurvivesTitleEdit`, `TestAcquireRecordedBranchNotSavedOnCASFailure` (lease). All pass. |
| R1: dropped-checkpoint identity is reused | Verified | `TestAcquireRecordedBranchUsesDroppedCheckpoint` (lease) and `TestIssueEditTitleEditRecordedBranchDroppedCheckpoint` (CLI: checkpoint → release → title edit → new base → approve → claim → stage) pass. A mutation that replaces `DroppedCheckpoint.Branch` with the title-derived name (via `go test -overlay`; no workspace file touched) fails both: `claim reserved "swarm/issue-1-renamed-task", want "swarm/issue-1-approved-task"`. |
| N2: a fork claim after a same-repo reservation gets `ForkBranchName` | Verified | `TestForkAcquireAfterRecordedBranchUsesForkBranchName` passes; it fails when the reservation is disabled. |
| AC2: `issue edit --dry-run` notes the branch stays as recorded; covered by a test | Verified | `TestIssueEditDryRunRecordedBranch` covers the recorded, missing, same-title, and active-claim cases, in text and JSON. It asserts state bytes are unchanged, there are no tracker writes, and the issue is unchanged. `TestIssueEditBackendGitHub` asserts the notice over the GitHub HTTP fixture. |

| Constraint: changelog fragment | Present | `changes/unreleased/218-stable-task-branch.md`. Its absence on the approved base could not be checked: there is no Git metadata in the sandbox. |
